draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Bhoothathankettu! The name means "monster fort", because people long ago believed a monster piled up the huge stones across the Periyar here. Today a modern dam sits alongside the old natural one.
draft.hungryLine: There's not much in the way of restaurants out here, so eat in Kothamangalam, about 10 km away, before or after.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk to the dam first, then trek through the forest to the old Bhoothathan Kettu, the original stone dam.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Take a boat out on the reservoir and let the forest do the rest.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The old dam isn't built the usual way. Large blocks of unshaped stone are piled on both sides of the Periyar.

legends.title: The monster's wall
legends.body: Legend says a Bhootham, a monster, built this dam out of rocks. That's where the name Bhoothathan Kettu comes from.

legends.title: An older name
legends.body: The Kothamangalam area nearby was once known as Malakhachira. It is a nice bit of local history to know.

tips.title: Go early for the birds.
tips.body: Pair the dam with the Thattekkad bird sanctuary, where exotic birds flock and rare species turn up.

tips.title: Wear proper shoes for the trek.
tips.body: The walk through the forest to the old Bhoothathan Kettu is the best part, and it's a real trek.

story.title: A natural dam
story.body: Huge unshaped stones blocked the Periyar here, forming a natural dam. Past generations believed a monster had built it.

story.title: Taming the Periyar
story.body: Dams went up across the Periyar at Edamalayar, Lower Periyar and Bhoothathankettu for hydroelectricity and irrigation. A modern dam was added beside the old one.

story.title: A picnic by the reservoir
story.body: The Bhoothathankettu Reservoir, also called the Thattekad Reservoir, is a favourite picnic spot. You can go boating and trek in the forest around it.
